title: Tamsin and the Salt
premise: Noor Hartwell, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist, has spent twenty years hiding her gift in Saltmere, a city where magic is outlawed and charms are sold as trinkets. When her blind date quotes a prophecy written a century before his birth, Noor discovers the book names her — and the date — as the thieves who will steal back the soul of Wren, a child sold to the court beneath the mountain. Hunted by Saltmere's witch-finders and betrayed by the prophecy's true author, Noor must choose between the loyalty she owes her hidden community and the truth that her own memory was the price paid to seal the bargain. In the end, she returns Wren's soul by surrendering her maps instead, and the long winter breaks over a city that finally remembers what it outlawed.
about_author: Vesper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year, and they insist this is not ominous.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Table
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She closes her charm shop and meets Corwin Ash for a blind date, sketching him out of habit — and realizes mid-sketch that his face matches an illustration she drew years ago in a map she never made. Beat: unease dressed as romance.

chapters.title: A Book That Waits
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following Corwin's quoted verse, she finds a sealed prophecy book in the archive beneath her shop; her own name is inked on its final page in handwriting that is unmistakably hers. Beat: dread of self-recognition.

chapters.title: Salt Laws
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. A witch-finder raids the date-night district; Corwin shields Noor and reveals he can read the salt-lines that mark magical debt. He knows more about the prophecy than he admits. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Child Without Weather
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She visits Wren, a neighbor's daughter whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain; the girl casts no shadow and no frost clings to her. The mother begs Noor for help. Beat: guilt crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn how Noor came to Saltmere with no past, no memories older than twenty years, and built a life from harmless trinkets. Beat: tenderness undercut by a hole she cannot name.

chapters.title: The Undermarket
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor and Corwin descend through a smuggler's tunnel into the Undermarket, where debts are traded like spices, and learn Wren's soul was purchased by the Gloam Court itself. Beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. A broker reveals the contract: the soul was payment for ending a previous winter, signed by someone named Hartwell — a century ago. Beat: betrayal, as Noor's own name surfaces in the wrong century.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Her cartography gift pulls her into a memory-map of Saltmere one hundred years past, where she watches herself — older, desperate — sign the contract. Beat: identity shattering.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Kindness
chapters.summary: Witch-finder Sera Voss's POV. Voss has tracked Noor for years but hesitates, because the prophecy book once belonged to her own grandmother. Beat: antagonist given a conscience.

chapters.title: Frostline
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The long winter begins early and unnaturally; streets freeze in patterns matching the prophecy's illustrations. Saltmere blames magic, and the hunts intensify. Beat: the city turning on its own.

chapters.title: The Hidden Congregation
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. He brings Noor to the underground community of concealed magicians who have protected her for twenty years — and who knew the truth of her contract all along. Beat: belonging poisoned by deception.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Her oldest friend Maren confesses she helped erase Noor's memory to protect the congregation, believing the winter would return if Noor remembered. Beat: fury and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Noor and Corwin's alternating POV. They flee the city through a pass only Noor can map, pursued by Voss and hunted by the mountain's own weather. Beat: trust rebuilt in small increments.

chapters.title: Court of Gloam
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach the Gloam Court, a cathedral of ice and candleless light, where the court's sovereign offers Noor a trade: her remaining memories for Wren's soul. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Century Bargain
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Corwin uncovers the court's ledger and learns the truth: the original winter never ended — it was merely deferred, and Wren's soul is collateral on a loan coming due. Beat: stakes redefined.

chapters.title: Voss at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. Voss arrives to arrest them but reads her grandmother's marginalia in the prophecy and understands the witch-finders were founded to enforce the court's contract, not to stop magic. Beat: allegiance inverted.

chapters.title: What Noor Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She recovers the erased memory: a century ago she tried to steal the soul back alone, failed, and chose oblivion rather than let the congregation die for her. Beat: compassion for her former self.

chapters.title: Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: Noor, Corwin, and Voss's POV braided together. The heist: they steal Wren's soul from the court's vault using Noor's maps as misdirection, triggering the court's awakening. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed by consequence.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The deferred century of winter descends all at once as they flee; Corwin is caught in the frost and begins to fade, his own name appearing in the ledger's debit column. Beat: sacrifice demanded.

chapters.title: The Price Rewritten
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the court's threshold, Noor refuses both trades and instead surrenders her life's work — every map of every unmapped realm — erasing the court's claim to any soul ever mapped or sold. Beat: climax; loyalty to people over truth to power.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The winter breaks; Corwin returns half-remembering her; Wren's shadow lengthens across the snow. Voss burns the witch-finders' charter. Beat: grief and grace in equal measure.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Salt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. In the recovered memories, Noor finds her true first name — Tamsin — and chooses to keep Noor anyway, opening a new shop that sells maps openly. The last page shows her drawing a door where the mountain used to be. Beat: wholeness chosen, not restored.
